name: FlashInfer
notable_features: A kernel library for LLM serving, not a serving engine: attention, sampling and fused-MoE primitives that other engines call into
JIT compilation with a cubin cache and a pluggable JIT cache provider, plus prebuilt flashinfer-cubin artifacts
Default attention backend for SGLang and selectable in vLLM, so it changes those engines' performance more than it provides a runtime of its own
Customizable attention plans and prefill/decode splits; paper at arXiv:2501.01005
hardware_caveats: CUDA-only and sm75+ only - it is explicitly unsupported below compute capability 7.5, which excludes Volta and older

Requires JIT compilation on first use, so cold start and cache-miss environments pay a compile cost; stale caches are a known failure mode and the documented fix is a forced reinstall plus deleting ~/.cache/flashinfer
Not an engine: you cannot serve a model with it alone. Scheduling is 'none' because it owns no scheduler
Kernels are tuned for NVIDIA's architecture; there is no HIP, ROCm, Metal or Vulkan path
When it misbehaves on sm75+ parts, the engines' documented fallback is to switch attention and sampling back to Triton and PyTorch
best_for: Squeezing attention and sampling throughput inside SGLang or vLLM on NVIDIA GPUs
Researching custom attention plans and sampling strategies against a real serving harness
As the default attention path when you have already committed to SGLang
avoid_for: Non-NVIDIA hardware, or NVIDIA parts below sm75
Environments where JIT compilation at runtime is unacceptable
Serving on its own - pair it with an engine
notes: supported_formats is essentially empty by design: it consumes tensors from a host engine rather than loading checkpoints. Included here because it is a genuine, widely deployed GPU inference component that changes engine performance characteristics, and because its sm75 floor is the kind of hardware boundary this knowledge base exists to record.
